items.author: Cointelegraph
items.context: Cointelegraph (JUST IN, con imágenes): según Elliptic, hackers vinculados a Corea del Norte han lavado al menos US$149 millones en bitcoin robados a Binance mediante transacciones coinjoin; el 90% de la actividad ocurrió desde el martes.
items.suggested_text:
$149M pushed through coinjoins in a matter of days is the part that matters: every mixing round thins the trail that firms like Elliptic can follow, and the window to freeze anything at an off-ramp closes fast.

It's also a reminder of where the target sits. Exchanges concentrate thousands of users' coins in hot wallets, which is exactly what state-backed groups are built to attack. Holding your own keys doesn't remove risk, it moves it to you: how the seed is generated, where it's stored, whether the signing device ever touches a network. That's the setup I walk through step by step here: https://x.com/ForecastQuant/status/2123585216740528526

The uncomfortable part isn't whether another exchange gets hit, but how many users only find out when withdrawals pause.
